Article Title: FSSAI puts influencers, celebrities on notice over food promotions
Article Text:
FSSAI warns influencers of legal action over unverified food claims

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: From "boosts immunity" to "rich in nutrients", food claims endorsed by celebrities and social media influencers are now under the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India's (FSSAI) scanner. In a significant move aimed at curbing misleading promotions, the regulator has warned influencers and celebrities that endorsing unverified food claims could invite legal action, even as it cracked down on manufacturers selling unsafe food products.The advisory comes at a time when food brands are increasingly relying on digital creators and celebrities to market health drinks, protein supplements, snacks and packaged foods to millions of consumers online. FSSAI has asked influencers to verify that every claim made by a brand is truthful, scientifically substantiated and compliant with food safety regulations before lending their name or credibility.The regulator said endorsements are more than advertisements because consumers often trust the people promoting them. It cautioned influencers against amplifying claims such as "boosts immunity" or "rich in nutrients" unless they are backed by evidence and permitted under food laws.Misleading food advertisements and endorsements, it said, can attract action under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, and the Food Safety and Standards (Advertising and Claims) Regulations, 2018.Alongside the advisory, FSSAI prohibited the manufacture, sale and distribution of food products made by M/s Shree Shyam Foods, M/s Bharat Food Products and M/s KDP Food Industry after government laboratories found their ghee and mustard oil products unsafe for consumption.The regulator also penalised Dharwad Mishra Pedha and Food Processing Industry in Karnataka after its Motichoor laddoos were found to contain Tartrazine at 2,670.5 mg/kg, more than 26 times the permissible limit of 100 mg/kg. Shree Chemfood Pvt Ltd of Gujarat was similarly penalised after samples of iodised salt were found to be substandard and misbranded.FSSAI has also urged consumers to report misleading food advertisements and celebrity endorsements through its Food Safety Connect platform.
Article Summary: Fssai warns influencers of legal action over unverified food claims. Fssai has asked influencers to verify that every claim made by a brand is truthful, scientifically substantiated and compliant with food safety regulations before lending their name or credibility.

Article Title: Gaps in Meta policy to protect copyright material, says judge
Article Text:
A content creator moved HC alleging that genuine creators such as him were denied access to the copyright tool

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Delhi high court Wednesday asked Meta to explain the criteria it follows to grant users access to its copyright management tool, Rights Manager, for Facebook and Instagram.A content creator moved HC alleging that genuine creators such as him were denied access to the copyright tool and, thus, were unable to protect their original content whose ownership was claimed by scammers using Rights Manager.Justice Anup J Bhambhani criticised the platform’s restrictive policy. “Why does everybody not have access to it then? It is like giving the key to the robber and not to the owner of the house,” it said.The judge said there appeared to be “some chinks in the armour, some loopholes” in the Meta policy on safeguarding the copyright material.Rights Manager enables pre-approved users to identify content uploaded on Facebook and Instagram and stake ownership as it permits them to monitor, block or act against such content.“Rights Manager is a video, audio and image-matching tool that we developed for rights holders of all sizes — from individual creators to media publishers, sports leagues, music labels and others — to identify and manage their content on Facebook and Instagram, including live videos,” the platform told the court.Meta submitted before HC that the copyright strikes against the plaintiff stood reversed and whatever content was removed has also been restored.It said the plaintiff’s accounts had never been suspended and remained accessible.HC then issued summons in the suit and posted the matter for hearing on Sept 24 along with a connected petition filed by another content creator.The second plea has alleged that the creator’s Instagram account was suspended following a copyright strike that was subsequently found to be false. The connected proceedings will also examine issues concerning the authority of social media platforms to suspend user profiles based on copyright infringement claims.
Article Summary: A content creator moved hc alleging that genuine creators such as him were denied access to the copyright tool. Justice anup j bhambhani criticised the platform’s restrictive policy. “it is like giving the key to the robber and not to the owner of the house,” it said.

Article Title: 5 indigenous small modular reactors targeted by 2033, Jitendra Singh tells LS
Article Text:
Union MoS Jitendra Singh speaks in the Lok Sabha during the Monsoon session of Parliament

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A key objective of the govt under the Nuclear Energy Mission is to develop and operationalise at least five indigenous small modular reactors by 2033, minister for department of atomic energy Jitendra Singh said in a written reply in the Lok Sabha on Wednesday.Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) is undertaking the design and development of indigenous SMR technologies, including the 220 MWe Bharat Small Modular Reactor (BSMR-200) and 55 MWe SMR-55 for power generation. BARC is also developing a high temperature gas cooled reactor (HTGCR) of up to 5 MW capacity, which can be coupled with a suitable thermochemical cycle for hydrogen production.Singh said India is steadily strengthening its indigenous nuclear energy ecosystem with a focus on advanced reactor technologies, SMRs, domestic manufacturing capabilities, private-sector participation and long-term utilisation of the country’s abundant thorium resources. The govt has adopted a two-pronged approach to accelerate nuclear capacity addition. This includes deployment of large indigenous reactors such as 700 MWe pressurised heavy water reactors (PHWRs) and advanced reactor designs at greenfield sites, alongside development and deployment of SMRs at brownfield locations, including retiring fossil-fuel-based power plants, captive plants for energy-intensive industries and off-grid applications in remote areas.The minister also highlighted continuing work of the Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research (IGCAR) in advancing the second stage of India’s nuclear power programme. IGCAR is pursuing multidisciplinary scientific research and advanced engineering development for sodium cooled fast breeder reactors and associated closed fuel-cycle facilities, technologies that remain a cornerstone of India’s long-term nuclear strategy.On thorium, Singh said India is pursuing its three-stage nuclear power programme, based on a closed fuel cycle, to optimise utilisation of its uranium resources and progressively harness its abundant thorium reserves. Thorium, being a fertile material, needs to be converted into fissile uranium-233 in a nuclear reactor before it can be used for energy generation.India has already undertaken sustained R&D towards thorium utilisation. Thorium Oxide (Thoria) pellets have been used in the initial cores of operating PHWRs, while Thoria-based fuels have also been irradiated in BARC research reactors. The irradiated Thoria pins have been reprocessed to obtain uranium-233, which has subsequently been fabricated as fuel for the KAMINI reactor at IGCAR, Kalpakkam. Singh said the Sustainable Harnessing and Advancement of Nuclear Energy for Transforming India (SHANTI) Act, 2025 has been enacted to enable wider participation of both public and private entities in the nuclear sector.
Article Summary: The govt under the nuclear energy mission is to develop and operationalise at least five indigenous small modular reactors by 2033. Bhabha atomic research centre (barc) is undertaking the design and development of indigenous smr technologies. The govt has adopted a two-pronged approach to accelerate nuclear capacity addition.

Article Title: IN-SPACe approved country’s first fully commercial earth observation sat constellation: Jitendra Singh
Article Text:
The consortium named Allied Orbits Private Limited is led by Pixxel Space India and includes Dhruva Space, PierSight Space and Satsure Analytics India

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Space regulator IN-SPACe has approved and signed under the PPP model an agreement with a private consortium for the country’s first indigenous, fully commercial earth observation constellation, with a view to enhancing the country’s space-based observation capabilities and building a self-reliant earth observation (EO) ecosystem in the country, minister for department of space Jitendra Singh informed Lok Sabha on Wednesday in response to a Parliament question.The consortium named Allied Orbits Private Limited is led by Pixxel Space India and includes Dhruva Space, PierSight Space and Satsure Analytics India. It will invest more than Rs 1,200 crore for setting up the constellation, which is to be developed and operationalised by 2029.The consortium will design, build, own and operate the 12-satellite constellation, which will have panchromatic, multispectral, hyperspectral and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) capabilities, supported by indigenous ground infrastructure. All satellites are to be manufactured domestically and launched on Indian launch vehicles, with mission control based in the country.The programme includes designing, fabrication, integration and the testing of EO satellites, including five ultra-high resolution optical satellites with 4 bands, 3 multispectral satellites with 8 bands, 2 hyperspectral optical satellites with 250 bands and 2 Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) satellites in X-band, by the Indian industry. The EO programme will use Indian launch vehicles (either private or Isro facilities) for placing the satellites into orbit. The programme also allows collaboration with academic and research institutions for capacity building and application development, the minister said.
Article Summary: The consortium named allied orbits private limited is led by pixxel space india. It will invest more than rs 1,200 crore for setting up the constellation, which is to be developed and operationalised by 2029. All satellites are to be manufactured domestically and launched on indian launch vehicles, with mission control based in the country.

Article Title: How Corporate India Is Investing In Climate & Environmental Resilience
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For years, environmental CSR in India was largely associated with tree plantation drives, cleanliness campaigns and occasional conservation projects. While those initiatives continue, companies are increasingly directing their CSR efforts towards something far more strategic. They’re strengthening climate resilience, securing water resources, promoting circular use of materials, and helping communities adapt to a warming world.The change reflects a growing realisation that environmental sustainability is no longer just about protecting nature. It is about protecting livelihoods, businesses, and the economy itself.Climate change is already affecting water availability, agriculture, supply chains, and industrial operations. As these risks intensify, Corporate India is beginning to see environmental CSR not as philanthropy but as an investment in long-term resilience.The scale of the challenge is enormous. India's draft Climate Finance Taxonomy estimates that the country will require around $2.5 trillion (Roughly an estimated Rs 2,50,00,000 crore or Rs 250 trillion) to meet its climate commitments by 2030, while climate adaptation alone could require investments of nearly Rs 56.7 trillion during the same period.These figures underline why resilience has become a business imperative as much as an environmental one.Increasingly, companies are aligning their CSR programmes with this new reality. Water has emerged as one of the biggest priorities.According to the Central Ground Water Board, India extracts 245.6 billion cubic metres (BCM) of groundwater annually, with 751 assessment units already categorised as over-exploited, 206 as critical and another 711 as semi-critical. Agriculture accounts for 87% of groundwater extraction, making water scarcity a concern that extends far beyond farms to industries, cities and supply chains.For CSR programmes, this has meant a shift from isolated water projects towards landscape-level interventions. Infosys, for instance, reports creating 40 lakes across its campuses with a combined rainwater storage capacity of 430 million litres, supported by 409 deep injection wells and complete recycling of wastewater.UltraTech Cement says its operations became 4.9 times water positive during FY2024-25 through rainwater harvesting, groundwater recharge, watershed management and recycling initiatives. Hindustan Zinc reports achieving 3.3 times water positivity while targeting a 50% reduction in freshwater consumption by 2030. ITC, meanwhile, has expanded watershed restoration and river basin stewardship programmes alongside improvements in water-use efficiency.The common thread running through these initiatives is that they benefit both communities and businesses. Restoring watersheds improves groundwater availability for nearby villages while also reducing water-related risks for industrial operations. Wastewater recycling lowers pressure on freshwater resources while helping industries operate more sustainably.The focus is also widening beyond water. Another emerging area for CSR is the circular economy, where companies seek to minimise waste and maximise the productive use of resources. Rather than viewing waste simply as something to be disposed of, businesses are increasingly investing in recycling, reuse and resource recovery.India's policy framework now covers plastics, batteries, e-waste, waste tyres, construction waste and several other waste streams under Extended Producer Responsibility rules. As of March 2026, registered recyclers had processed 417.6 lakh metric tonnes of waste, generating nearly 342 lakh metric tonnes of EPR certificates. The government has also introduced a Rs 1,500 crore incentive scheme to promote recycling of critical minerals such as lithium, nickel and cobalt.Corporate initiatives are increasingly reflecting this transition. Tata Steel reported recycling around 4.2 million tonnes of scrap during FY2024-25. Infosys diverted 98% of its waste away from landfills, while Hindustan Zinc is working towards achieving near-zero waste to landfill by 2030 through greater reuse and recycling. These examples demonstrate how environmental investments can reduce raw material consumption, lower disposal costs, and improve resource security.CSR is also beginning to support innovation rather than only funding conventional projects. Technology-led solutions are emerging as an important area of investment. Digital Paani, featured in NITI Aayog's Frontier Tech Repository, uses Internet of Things-based automation to optimise wastewater treatment plants. The platform has been deployed at more than 40 facilities, treating over 90 million litres of wastewater every day.In agriculture, Kheyti's "greenhouse-in-a-box" model has demonstrated how climate-smart farming can improve resilience. According to the study cited in the report, participating farmers recorded a 73% increase in income, 58% lower crop losses, 67% lower water consumption, and significantly lower fertiliser use. Satellite-enabled platforms such as SatSure are also helping govts, financial institutions and agribusinesses assess climate risks and improve decision-making using artificial intelligence and Earth observation data.The evolution of environmental CSR reflects a broader shift in corporate thinking. Earlier, environmental spending was often evaluated through the number of trees planted or awareness campaigns organised.Today, companies are increasingly asking whether their investments improve water security, strengthen ecosystems, reduce resource consumption, and help communities withstand climate shocks.The approach also aligns more closely with business priorities. Healthier watersheds mean more reliable water supplies. Circular resource use reduces dependence on virgin materials. Climate-resilient agriculture strengthens rural livelihoods while improving supply-chain stability. Investments in environmental resilience, therefore, generate benefits that extend beyond compliance or corporate reputation.
Article Summary: For years, environmental csr in india was largely associated with tree plantation drives. But companies are increasingly directing their csr efforts towards something far more strategic. They’re strengthening climate resilience, securing water resources, promoting circular use of materials.

Article Title: Medical device industry seeks rethink of draft law, urges separate regulatory body
Article Text:
The draft aims to repeal the existing Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940. (Representative Image)

NEW DELHI: The domestic medical device industry, along with hospitals and healthcare providers, has urged govt to re-examine the Draft Drugs, Medical Devices & Cosmetics Bill, 2026."The Bill in its present form, does not provide the regulatory foundation required for India's medical devices sector to grow, innovate, and compete globally", an industry expert told TOI.The draft aims to repeal the existing Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, and consolidate laws related to import, manufacture, distribution and sale of drugs, medical devices and cosmetics, to ensure their quality, safety and efficacy.In a letter to govt, the associations say that the draft bill, in its current form, treats medical devices as an adjunct to pharmaceuticals, despite clear scientific, engineering, and regulatory distinction between the two.Medical devices are engineering products, and should not be clubbed with pharmaceuticals, the letter says, adding the draft Bill continues to use drug-centric terminology such as "adulterated", "spurious"."misbranded", and applies pharma-style criminalisation to engineering deviations.Globally, medical devices are regulated through risk-based conformity assessment and quality management systems.Further, the Bill does not provide for a dedicated regulatory authority for medical devices, despite repeated recommendations.In 2023, the Association of Indian Medical Device Industry argued that proposed overarching legislation (such as the Drugs, Medical Devices and Cosmetics draft) fails the domestic sector by continuing to regulate medical devices as "drugs" under a joint framework, instead of establishing an independent, specialized regulatory body.Administrative enforcement including recalls, corrective actions, civil penalties-- should replace imprisonment for technical lapses, the letter by 11 associations including Aimed, AHPI (Association of Healthcare Providers India), ADMI (Association of Diagnostics Manufacturers) and Patient Safety and Access Initiative, says.The Bill 2026 applies uniform penalties across all device classes, from low-risk surgical instruments to high-risk implants, contrary to global norms.It does not clearly recognise key medical device standards covering areas such as biocompatibility, usability and software safety.While the draft has been circulated to various ministries and departments, key stakeholders, including industry associations, manufacturers and hospital bodies, have not been adequately involved in the process, the industry executive said, adding it appears inconsistent with the pre-legislative consultation process.
Article Summary: The draft aims to repeal the existing drugs and cosmetics act, 1940. The domestic medical device industry has urged govt to re-examine the draft drugs, medical devices & cosmetics bill, 2026. "the bill in its present form, does not provide the regulatory foundation required for india's medical devices sector to grow, innovate, and compete globally," an industry expert said.

Article Title: Will Jeanie Buss keep her Lakers role after record $12.5 billion ownership shake-up?
Article Text:
Jeanie Buss. Image via: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-USA TODAY Sports

Jeanie Buss' Lakers role revealed after $12.5 billion sale

How a Vegas expansion pitch turned into a $12.5 billion Lakers deal

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jeanie Buss will remain governor of the Los Angeles Lakers even as the franchise changes hands again, this time in a record $12.5 billion sale from Mark Walter to an ownership group led by Bob Iger and Josh Kushner. The deal, reported Wednesday, comes just over a year after Walter bought the team from the Buss family for $10 billion.Iger confirmed to Khobi Price of the California Post that his group intends to honor the arrangement Walter made with Buss in that original sale, which guaranteed her the governor role for at least five years.Buss stepping away from day-to-day control of the Lakers seemed like a real possibility once word broke that Walter was selling. Instead, the incoming ownership group is keeping the arrangement Walter struck with the Buss family intact."We have enormous respect and appreciation for Jeanie, her father and what they've contributed to this franchise," Iger said. "And we have every intention to honor the agreement that was made between Mark and Jeanie. If things change, they'll change, but we're going into this with enormous respect and appreciation for who she is and what she represents in the organization."That last line matters. Iger isn't calling the arrangement permanent. He's calling it intact for now, with room to revisit it later.Iger and Kushner weren't shopping for the Lakers. They were chasing a different opportunity entirely, an ownership stake in the NBA's potential expansion franchise in Las Vegas, when Walter's willingness to sell reached them last weekend."We were involved in pursuing the new franchise in Vegas," Iger said. "And while that happened, it was suggested to us that maybe Mark Walter would be interested in selling his stake in the Lakers. And we immediately decided that given the value of the franchise and the iconic nature of the team, that we would be really smart to pursue it. The deal came together in three days.""It's that simple," he added.Three business days is a fast turnaround for a $12.5 billion transaction involving one of the NBA's flagship franchises, and Iger doesn't sound like someone still catching his breath from it."Grateful, appreciative, excited to own something that's as iconic as the LA Lakers," Iger said. "Josh and I are avid NBA fans. And to have an opportunity to own not just any NBA team, but the LA Lakers is…it's extraordinary from a life experience perspective and business perspective. It's still sinking in. We're very excited."Iger has already made two calls that matter. He's spoken with Buss, and he's spoken with head coach JJ Redick, a relationship that dates back to Redick's years with the Clippers from 2013 to 2017, when Iger held Clippers season tickets. One call he hasn't made yet stands out, Luka Doncic, the franchise's current star and the player any new ownership group needs on board.Iger isn't pretending to have the Lakers' future mapped out. He and Kushner went from pursuing an expansion team in Las Vegas to owning the Lakers in roughly 72 hours, and he said as much when asked what comes next, that no concrete plans exist yet beyond honoring what's already in place.For now, that means Jeanie Buss stays in her role, at least through the term Walter guaranteed her. Iger's own words leave the only real question hanging over the deal: how long "for now" actually lasts.
Article Summary: Bob iger and josh kushner bought the los angeles lakers for a record $12.5 billion. The deal comes just over a year after mark walter bought the team from the buss family for $10 billion. Jeanie buss will remain in her role as governor, at least for now.

McGregor turned his fame into a global business brand, while Khabib has mainly stayed connected to MMA through promotions, coaching, endorsements and other ventures.The exact net worth figures are estimates, not official financial statements, so different outlets give different numbers. Some estimates put his wealth around $40 million, while Celebrity Net Worth lists it at $25 million in 2026.Unlike McGregor, Khabib did not have a huge crossover boxing event or a billion-dollar-style consumer brand deal, so his wealth has grown at a different pace.The answer comes down to business scale. McGregor turned his UFC fame into a worldwide celebrity brand and used that attention to build companies, secure major endorsements and land the Mayweather fight.Khabib became one of the greatest MMA fighters ever, but his business activity has remained more closely tied to fighting, coaching and the regional market. That does not mean he has been unsuccessful. A fortune of tens of millions of dollars is still enormous.For now, though, McGregor remains far ahead financially, with a 2026 net worth estimate of about $200 million compared with Khabib’s estimated $25 million to $45 million.

Article Title: Buffalo Bills address viral “obstructed seat” photos that left fans furious over new $2.1B stadium
Article Text:
Buffalo Bills address viral “obstructed seat” photos that left fans furious over new $2.1B stadium(Getty)

Buffalo Bills explain their position as viral seat photos create early controversy around new Highmark Stadium

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Buffalo Bills expected fans to leave the new Highmark Stadium talking about the atmosphere. Instead, many left talking about blocked views.Photos from Saturday’s Blue and Red practice spread rapidly across social media. Fans showed railings, stair structures and overhangs cutting into their sightlines. Within hours, the excitement around the $2.2 billion stadium turned into a heated debate among Bills fans.More than 51,000 fans attended the first public event at the new stadium, and many praised the steep seating bowl and the energy inside the building. However, the viral photos quickly changed the conversation.Several personal seat license holders compared the actual view from their seats with the virtual renderings they saw before buying. Some felt the real experience did not match what they expected after spending thousands of dollars on seat licenses.The Bills responded by acknowledging the feedback and promising further review. A team spokesperson told Sportico that Saturday’s practice served as an important test for the new facility.“Saturday’s practice was a great opportunity to test the new stadium,” the spokesperson said. “We are currently addressing internal and external feedback regarding the facility’s operation following the first event.We’ll uutilisethe next six weeks to refine any details as we prepare for the home opener on Thursday, Sept. 17.”That statement became the clearest indication that the organisation plans to make adjustments before the regular-season debut against the Detroit Lions.The controversy grew because some of the images reached millions of people online. One Associated Press photo from a seat not used for Bills games drew millions of views on X, while a compilation of obstructed-view photos spread even further. Some fans claimed the railings affected the first several rows across many upper-deck sections.At the same time, other supporters pushed back and shared positive experiences from their visit. According to reports, the team has heard from fewer than 1% of personal seat license holders regarding sightline concerns.The new stadium represents a major project for Buffalo. The Bills, Erie County and New York State agreed to the stadium deal in 2022, with $850 million in public funding helping keep the franchise in Western New York. The previous stadium opened in 1973.Architectural firm Populous designed the venue with a steep seating bowl intended to bring the upper deck closer to the field. Open concourses were also designed to maintain views of the action from many areas of the building.The team chose a canopy structure instead of a full dome. The canopy aims to protect roughly two-thirds of the seats from weather while also helping trap crowd noise inside the stadium.The Bills exceeded expectations in seat-license sales, generating about $260 million from more than 53,000 PSLs. Virtual seat views played a significant role in that sales process, which is why the comparison between renderings and real-world views became such a sensitive issue.Ticketmaster identifies some locations as obstructed-view seats, but several buyers believe the warning did not fully reflect the actual experience.Most early reviews of the new Highmark Stadium remain positive. Still, the viral seat photos created an early public-relations challenge. Bills fans now want more than explanations. They want proof that the vast majority of seats deliver the clear view promised during the long wait for the team’s new home.
Article Summary: Buffalo bills address viral “obstructed seat” photos that left fans furious over new $2.1b stadium. Fans showed railings, stair structures and overhangs cutting into their sightlines. Bills responded by acknowledging the feedback and promising further review.

Article Title: Who is Gautam Rangarajan? Indian-origin strategist appointed to key role by UK PM Andy Burnham

Indian-origin strategist Gautam Rangarajan.

Who is Gautam Rangarajan ?

What will Gautam Rangarajan do at No. 10?

Burnham's government overhaul

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has appointed Indian-origin strategist and former BBC executive Gautam Rangarajan as an Expert Adviser on Structure and Process in a newly created role at 10 Downing Street.Rangarajan, who brings decades of experience in strategy, organisational transformation and media, is set to take up the position this week.Rangarajan is a senior strategist and media executive with more than two decades of experience across media, creative industries and public service broadcasting.Before his new government role, he spent more than 30 years at the BBC, beginning his career as a radio music producer and eventually rising to become the broadcaster's Group Director for Strategy and Performance.His experience includes developing strategy in rapidly changing markets, leading large-scale transformation initiatives and handling complex policy and financial negotiations.The exact details of Rangarajan's responsibilities are yet to be outlined. However, the UK PM's office said his appointment draws on his experience in corporate strategy and transformation.His role comes as Burnham undertakes a broader restructuring of the machinery of government, including the creation of the Office for the Prime Minister and Cabinet.Rangarajan is expected to play a role in the planned transformation at the heart of the British government.Away from strategy and public service, Rangarajan also has a creative side. He describes himself as a professional choral singer and music producer, alongside his work in corporate strategy and organisational transformation.The appointment comes as Burnham reshapes his government following his recent rise to the role of Labour Party leader and Prime Minister.His administration has announced structural changes, including the launch of No. 10 North in Manchester and the creation of the Office for the Prime Minister and Cabinet.While the full scope of Rangarajan's new role remains unclear, his appointment places the former BBC executive at the centre of the UK government's planned transformation.

Google Pixel 11 series has been launched. The company has officially taken the wraps off its next-generation Pixel lineup at its “Made by Google” hardware event, bringing three new phones: the Google Pixel 11, Google Pixel 11 Pro and Google Pixel 11 Pro XL, with a new in-house chip, a powerful security setup and a fresh round of AI features built around Gemini. The company has also launched the Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold, Google Pixel Watch 5 (in two sizes), a new colour of the Google Pixel Bunds Pro 2 and a bunch of accessories, including PixelSnap Ring Stand and PixelSnap charger with stand. Here's a complete breakdown of what is new and what it will cost you in India.The Google Pixel 11 starts at Rs 89,999 for the base 256GB model that comes with 12GB RAM. The Pixel 11 Pro price in India starts at Rs 1,19,999 for the base 256GB and the Pixel 11 Pro XL price in India starts at Rs 1,34,999. This means that the Pixel 11 series gets a Rs 10,000 price hike across models.Pre-orders for the series are now open through Google's own store as well as partner retailers with devices going on sale fromColour options also differ across the lineup: the Google Pixel Pro and Google Pixel Pro XL come in Canyon, Olive, Fog and a matte Obsidian finish, while the standard Google Pixel 11 gets its own palette of Frost, Pistachio, Hibiscus and Obsidian.All three phones stick with Google’s familiar Pixel design language, but the Pro models get a notably brighter, sharper screen. The Pixel 11 Pro comes with a 6.3-inch Super Actua display, while the Pro XL steps up to a larger 6.8-inch panel with both offering adaptive refresh rate that scales between 1Hz and 120Hz. The standard Pixel 11 gets a slightly smaller Actua display with a 60-120Hz range instead.Peak brightness on the Pro models can hit up to 3,600 nits, while the standard Pixel 11 tops out at 3,000 nits. All three models use Corning's Gorilla Glass Victus 2 for protection, with the Pro models adding an anti-scratch shield on top. One of the most highlighting changes in the phones is HiLight – an array of ambient LED lights built around the camera’s flash to give you light-based communications on the back of the phone.When your phone is face down, HiLight gently glows to give you a visual cue to pick up your phone, or stay in the moment.When it comes to performance and security, powering the entire lineup is Google’s new Tensor G6 chip, paired with a Titan M3 security coprocessor across all three models. Google is pitching this as a meaningful jump in on-device security, with a multi-layered setup that includes quantum-safe secure boot built directly into the hardware.Google Pixel phones have led the cameras department when it comes to point-and-shoot photography. The Google Pixel 11 Pro and Google Pixel 11 Pro XL share an identical camera setup: a 50MP wide lens, a 48MP ultrawide camera with macro focus, and a 48MP telephoto lens offering 5x optical zoom and up to 120x Pro Zoom. The standard Pixel 11 gets a slightly toned-down system: a 48MP wide camera, a 13MP ultrawide lens, and a 10.8MP telephoto sensor capped at 30x Super Zoom.On the front, the Pro models get a 42MP selfie camera, compared to 10.5MP on the standard Pixel 11. All three models support Google's usual suite of computational photography tools, including Night Sight, Astrophotography, Magic Eraser, Best Take, and the newer Edit with Ask Photos feature, which lets you make edits using natural-language prompts.Talking about battery, charging and durability, all three phones promise over 30 hours of battery life, backed by battery capacities ranging from 4,850mAh on the Pixel 11 Pro to up to 5,115mAh on the larger Google Pixel 11 Pro XL. All three also support Pixelsnap wireless charging at up to 25W, and come with an IP68 rating for dust and water resistance.Coming to the AI features and software, every model in the lineup ships with Gemini Intelligence built in, powered by Google's on-device Gemini Nano model. That includes access to Gemini Live for real-time conversational AI, along with Magic Cue, a feature designed to proactively surface relevant information based on what's happening on your screen. Google is also backing the lineup with a lengthy software commitment with all three phones are promised seven years of OS updates, security patches and Pixel Drop feature updates, running on Android 17 out of the box.

Article Title: TSMC and Taiwan researchers engineered an interface only 0.42 nanometers thick to improve next-generation MoS2 transistors
Article Text:
Representational AI photo

Focus on Atomic Boundary

Why interface matters

Science Daily photo

0.42-nanometre buffer layer

Relevance for future chips

Researchers from Taiwan's National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University (NYCU) and TSMC Corporate Research have developed a new way to improve transistors made from atomically thin materials. They focuses on the tiny boundary where two materials meet, which allowed them to build transistors with an extremely thin insulating layer while maintaining strong electrical performance.According to Science Daily, atomically thin semiconductors have been studied for more than a decade because some can be just one atom thick while still showing useful electrical properties. Such materials could allow transistors to become smaller, faster and more energy efficient than conventional silicon-based devices.However, making these very thin transistors work well has been difficult. One major problem involves the gate dielectric, an extremely thin insulating layer that helps control the movement of electrons. Making it thinner can improve transistor control, but when it is placed on an atomically thin semiconductor, problems can develop at the boundary between the two materials. These can interfere with electron movement and reduce performance.The new study, published in Nature Electronics, addresses this problem by engineering the atomic interface between the semiconductor and the insulating layer.The NYCU team worked with TSMC Corporate Research to engineer the narrow region where the two materials meet. Instead of focusing only on finding a new semiconductor, the researchers changed the interface itself.The team used monolayer molybdenum disulfide, or MoS2, as the semiconductor. A monolayer is a material that is only one layer of atoms thick. The researchers first placed an ultrathin epitaxial aluminium layer directly on the MoS2.They then oxidised the aluminium to create an aluminium oxide layer about 0.42 nanometres thick. After this, they added a high-κ hafnium oxide gate dielectric, an insulating material that can provide strong electrical control while remaining very thin.The 0.42-nanometre aluminium oxide layer acted as a buffer between the MoS2 and hafnium oxide. It created a smoother surface, helping the hafnium oxide grow more uniformly, while also reducing unwanted electrical interactions between the two materials."For many years, efforts to improve atomically thin transistors have largely focused on discovering better semiconductor materials," said Professor Wen-Hao Chang, the study's corresponding author from NYCU. "Our research shows that the atomic interface between materials can be just as important. By engineering that boundary, we were able to reduce one of the fundamental trade-offs that has limited two-dimensional transistors for many years," he added.Atomically thin semiconductors create a particular challenge because their surfaces do not have dangling bonds. This makes it difficult to grow an extremely thin dielectric layer evenly across the surface.Standard deposition methods can leave gaps and defects at the interface. These can create electrical disorder and reduce carrier mobility, which refers to how easily electrons move through a material.Researchers have explored different dielectric materials, molecular seed layers and other oxide deposition methods. However, achieving a very thin equivalent oxide thickness, strong electrostatic control and high carrier mobility at the same time remains difficult.The challenge is especially important for wafer-scale CVD-grown monolayer MoS2. CVD, or chemical vapour deposition, is a method used to produce thin material layers over a larger area.The researchers' approach was to redesign the interface rather than replace the semiconductor or gate dielectric. They placed the ultrathin epitaxial aluminium layer on monolayer MoS2 and oxidised it to produce the 0.42-nanometre aluminium oxide layer. The high-κ hafnium oxide was then added on top.The team built short-channel top-gate transistors using CVD-grown monolayer MoS2. The devices had an equivalent oxide thickness of about one nanometre.Tests showed low leakage current and minimal hysteresis. Hysteresis refers to unwanted differences in a transistor's electrical response depending on its previous operating condition.The transistors reached a maximum transconductance of 0.45 mS μm-1, with channel lengths of about 100 nanometres. Transconductance measures how strongly a transistor's current responds when the gate voltage changes.The devices combined a very thin dielectric with strong electrical control and continued carrier transport, a combination that has been difficult to achieve in atomically thin transistors.The findings highlight the growing importance of interfaces as transistor components become smaller. When materials are only a few atomic layers thick, the region where two materials meet can strongly affect how the device performs."When transistor components become only a few atomic layers thick, the interface is no longer simply the boundary between materials, it becomes an active part of the device," said Professor Tsung-En Lee, the study's corresponding author. "Learning to engineer these interfaces with atomic precision opens new opportunities for designing future semiconductor devices that would be difficult to achieve by changing individual materials alone," professor Lee added.The researchers believe the approach could contribute to future two-dimensional electronics. Using CVD-grown monolayer MoS2 also brings the work closer to materials and processes that could eventually be considered for wafer-scale manufacturing.
Article Summary: Researchers from taiwan's national yang ming chiao tung university have developed a new way to improve transistors made from atomically thin materials. They focuses on the tiny boundary where two materials meet, which allowed them to build transistors with an extremely thin insulating layer.

Article Title: FDA clears hearing aid feature on Samsung Galaxy Buds
Article Text:
Samsung introduced the Personal Sound Amplification Product (PSAP) feature on Galaxy Buds+ in 2020

Samsung announced that its Galaxy Buds Hearing Aid feature has received US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) clearance, enabling compatible Galaxy Buds to serve as an over-the-counter (OTC) hearing aid, offering users 18 years and older a convenient solution for addressing perceived mild to moderate hearing loss. Users can also diagnose their hearing with the Galaxy Buds Hearing Test feature, which is registered as a Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) and provides medical-grade results.Commenting on the launch, Hon Pak, Senior Vice President and Head of the Digital Health Team for the Mobile eXperience (MX) Business at Samsung Electronics said “Hearing health is a vital component of our overall well-being, profoundly impacting how we communicate, connect with loved ones and engage with the world,” adding “With the latest clearance from the FDA, we are expanding access to hearing support and making proactive care effortless by integrating the Hearing Test and Hearing Aid functionality directly into the Galaxy Buds. ”Samsung introduced a Personal Sound Amplification Product (PSAP) feature on Galaxy Buds+ in 2020. The PSAP feature was clinically validated in 2021 as effective support for daily communication for those with hearing loss.To develop this new OTC solution, Samsung collaborated closely with the National Acoustic Laboratories (NAL) and Samsung Medical Center (SMC). The resulting technology is backed by robust clinical validation studies conducted at Vanderbilt University Medical Center, San Jose State University and the University of Memphis.Based on those results, the Hearing Aid feature amplifies the sounds users have difficulty hearing — such as high frequencies, surrounding whispers and distant voices — personalized to each user’s hearing profile.Samsung said the hearing aid also supports additional advanced features typically found in premium hearing aids, such as noise elimination and beamforming, which help focus sounds in front of the user and suppress background noise. The Hearing Aid and Hearing Test features will be available on Galaxy Buds 3 Pro and Galaxy Buds 4 Pro in the US and select approved markets in Q4 2026.
Article Summary: Samsung announced that its galaxy buds hearing aid feature has received us food and drug administration (fda) clearance. The feature will enable compatible galaxy bud's to serve as an over-the-counter (otc) hearing aid, offering users 18 years and older a convenient solution for addressing perceived mild to moderate hearing loss.
